canonicalExplanation.summary: This capstone ties the course together. A **collaborative repository** needs more than Git access. It needs **written agreements**: a **CONTRIBUTING** guide with setup steps, how issues are claimed, branch naming, the PR template, **who reviews what** (CODEOWNERS), which **checks are required**, how releases are **tagged**, how to report **security** issues privately (SECURITY.md), and how people communicate. You'll deliver one change end to end: scoped issue, branch, commits, PR, review, green required checks, integration and a tag, all traceable. The goal is a project where a newcomer can contribute without asking anyone how things work.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A new contributor gets access to a repository with no README setup section, no issue labels and no idea which checks matter. They spend two days guessing, then open a 40-file PR that nobody knows how to review. A new contributor follows documented setup, claims a scoped issue, opens a focused branch and PR, responds to review, and sees the exact checks required for merge. In this lesson you'll deliver and explain a tagged collaborative change from scoped issue through passing reviewed integration.

Is collaboration now predictable?", "options": ["Yes, everyone can contribute", "No: without documented flow, review ownership and required checks, everyone guesses"], "answer": 1, "why": "Access lets people push; agreements make the results predictable and safe."}

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Issues, pull requests and review**, **Debugging and quality automation**, **Continuous integration pipeline**, **Secret prevention and response** and **Restore, revert, reset and reflog**.

sections.heading: The model: a documented path from issue to tag
sections.body:
```text
repo/
  README.md             setup: clone, npm ci, npm test, npm start.
  CONTRIBUTING.md       claim an issue, branch naming, commit style, PR checklist.
  .github/
    CODEOWNERS          src/payments/ @payments-team  (required reviewers).
    pull_request_template.md   why, what, tests, risk.
    workflows/ci.yml    lint, test, build (required on main).
  SECURITY.md           report vulnerabilities privately, never in public issues.
  .env.example          placeholders only.
```

```bash
git fetch && git switch -c fix/57-trailing-comma origin/main
# commits... npm test
git push -u origin fix/57-trailing-comma   # PR: "closes #57", template filled.
# review -> fix-up commits -> re-review -> required checks green -> squash merge.
git switch main && git pull --ff-only
git tag -a v1.3.1 -m "Fix trailing-comma parsing (#57)" && git push origin v1.3.1
```

```reveal
{"prompt": "What's the \"safe escalation path\"?", "answer": "A documented way to raise problems: who to ask when blocked, how to report a security issue privately, and what to do if main breaks (for example, revert first, then investigate)."}
```

sections.heading: Traceability check

includes: Document setup, issue flow, branching, review ownership, required checks, releases and escalation.
Deliver one traceable change from scoped issue to reviewed, tested, tagged integration.
excludes: Large-scale governance and multi-repo release trains.

outcomes: Deliver and explain a tagged collaborative change from scoped issue through passing reviewed integration.

examples.title: A new contributor's first merged change
examples.situation: A new contributor follows documented setup, claims a scoped issue, opens a focused branch and PR, responds to review, and sees the exact checks required for merge.
walkthrough: **Follows documented setup and claims a scoped issue:** README steps work on a clean clone; they comment on #57 and get assigned.
**Opens a focused branch and PR, responds to review:** fix/57-trailing-comma, template filled, one blocker fixed in a follow-up commit.
**Sees the exact checks required for merge:** lint, test and build are required; after merge the maintainer will tag v1.3.1.
examples.result: The newcomer's first change lands in a day, fully traceable from issue to tag.

examples.title: The broken main at 5 pm
examples.situation: A merge breaks main just before the end of the day. Nobody knows who should act.
walkthrough: CONTRIBUTING says: revert first, then investigate.
The on-call maintainer opens a revert PR; required checks pass; it merges.
An issue records the cause and the follow-up fix.
examples.result: Main is green again in minutes, with a clear record of what happened.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Installing Git and granting repository access is enough to make collaboration predictable and safe.
misconceptions.correction: Predictable collaboration needs documented setup, issue and branch flow, review ownership, required checks, release practice and escalation paths. Tools alone don't create agreements.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening story, why did the newcomer spend two days guessing?

analogy.example: A collaborative repo is like **a shared community kitchen**. Having a key (access) isn't enough. You need the posted rules: how to book a slot (claim an issue), where things go (branches), who checks hygiene (review), the inspection before serving (required checks), and who to call if something catches fire (escalation).
limitations: Kitchens rarely keep full records; repos can trace everything.
New cooks learn fastest from written rules.

nearTransfer.prompt: For a sandbox repository, write README setup steps, a CONTRIBUTING guide, a PR template and a SECURITY note. Ask a partner to follow them from a clean clone and record every question they had to ask.
scaffold: Test setup yourself on a clean clone first.
expectedEvidence: Every question answered in the docs afterwards.

farTransfer.prompt: With a partner, deliver one change end to end in a sandbox: scoped issue, branch, commits, PR from template, review with at least one blocker, required CI checks, squash merge and annotated tag. Then write a short report tracing the tag back to the issue.
scaffold: Use branch protection with required checks.
expectedEvidence: All required checks passed on the merged head.

remediation.explanation: Test your project's collaboration docs like code: **a newcomer, a clean clone, and only the written instructions.** Every question they ask is a missing line.

recap.summary: To deliver a tagged collaborative change, document setup, issue and branch flow, review ownership, required checks, releases and escalation, then take one scoped issue through a focused branch, reviewed PR, passing required checks, integration and an annotated tag, keeping every link traceable.
